labels.label: lem:gluing-estimate
labels.notes: Unmarked and partial, as the dispatch requires. These are lemmas, not the anchor. CONCLUSION (gluing_estimate, Gluing.lean:535–593) against eq:gluing-estimate (l.651–655). The statement is m·Vol(Σ,g)^{2/N} ≤ −F^{(β)}_g(u) + y·(volBar/Vol(Σ,h))^{(N−2)/N}, together with y·(volBar/Vol(Σ,h))^{(N−2)/N} ≤ 0. The constants, the exponents 2/N and (N−2)/N, the sign of F, the ratio Vol(Σ̄,h̄)/Vol(Σ,h̄), and 'the last term is non-positive' all match the paper. M.F g β u is traceSobolevQuot = (a_N‖∇u‖² + Σ_j β_j‖tr u‖²_{L^{p♯}(B_j)})/‖u‖²_{L^{p*}(Σ)}, which is l.611 with any real β, so it covers β_j = YB < 0. The intermediate steps are the printed ones. boundary_term_le is l.670, glue_upper is eq:glue-upper (l.674–676), and glue_lower is eq:glue-lower (l.660–661), obtained from the strict kobayashi through ConformalLaw. normSq_pStar_conformal and normSq_pSharp_conformal are the two identities of l.680, proved from IsConformal and DensityMeasurable, not carried. EHB is l.313 and the cap's action is l.665–666. On the toy witness the estimate holds with equality (LHS = RHS = −2^{2/3}), so it is not slack. FORMS. gluing_estimate takes any m ≤ 0 with m ≤ R_g a.e. and any β with BoundaryYamabe. Both are generalisations. lem_gluing_estimate has the printed m = kobM and the printed ∃u, witnessed by u = ψ|_Σ. gluing_estimate_YB has β_j = (F.piece j).YB (gj j), i.e. YB_[g_j](D_j) read through the conformal law, as the strict Y is. It reads '> −∞' as BddBelow, which is needed because Real.sInf of an unbounded set is 0, and it derives BoundaryYamabe by YB_le_EHB. CARRIED HYPOTHESES, one by one. (1) IsConformal (h = u^{4/(N−2)}g, u > 0) together with IsYamabeMetric (R_h̄ = c a.e. on Σ and on each D_j, c = y·volBar^{−2/N}) is thm:yamabe (b) as used at l.658. y is a real standing for Y_[ḡ](Σ̄), and the REPORT discloses this as a question. The lemma therefore holds for every CSC h̄ with R ≤ 0, and that includes the Yamabe metrics, so Lean ≥ paper. (2) BoundaryYamabe, β_j ≤ EHB(D_j, h̄|_{D_j}), is the printed step 'by definition of the boundary Yamabe constant' (l.663–666). (3) MeanCurvatureFlip, H^Σ_h = −H^{D_j}_h̄∘glue a.e. on B_j, is l.663. (4) ConformalLaw, EH(Σ,h)·‖u‖²_{L^{p*}(Σ,g)} = confAction g u, is eq:conformal-energy-bdry (l.326–328) verbatim, with φ = u and g̃ = h. It is an identity, not an inequality. It is genuinely needed: CurvedMetric's R and H are free data (Kobayashi.lean:118–125), so without it EH(Σ,h) has no link to u. It is also not stronger than the paper: the paper uses the same law, inside lem:kobayashi (a) at l.660. (5) BoundaryMatch, (bvol_h j).map (glue j) = bvol_{cap j} 0, is the geometric fact that B_j = ∂D_j carries the single induced metric h̄|_{B_j}, which is behind A_j := Vol(B_j, h̄) (l.663). It is genuinely needed, because D_j lives on its own carrier Y, and integral_flip and area_match cannot move ∫H or A_j across without it. A pushforward identity is exactly what the smooth geometry gives, so it is no stronger. (6) The trace and measurability conditions hold for smooth u and g: htr (tr u = val u a.e. on B_j), hum, hut and DensityMeasurable. So do vol_g ≠ 0, bvol_g j ≠ 0 and the IsFiniteMeasure instances. None of these hypotheses contains the conclusion. The upper bound comes out of the chain IsYamabeMetric + BoundaryYamabe + flip + match, the lower bound out of the strict Hölder/Kobayashi argument. JOINT SATISFIABILITY. toy_gluing_estimate (l.1008–1062) is genuine. It calls Filling.gluing_estimate itself, every explicit hypothesis is discharged, and m = c = −1 and y = −volBar^{2/3} < 0 are non-degenerate. Its β_0 = EHB(D_0, toyCurved) = −2, though, so it does not witness β = c_N, and it does not witness gluing_estimate_YB's extra inputs. The auditor closed both gaps by probe (see build.details and minor finding 1). A model note, not a finding: no IsFiniteMeasure is asked of the pieces' volumes, so for non-geometric data Vol(D_j, h̄).toReal could be a junk 0. The SCOPE sentence 'every quotient in the chain is genuine' is still true, and compact D_j make this harmless.

labels.label: thm:upper-bound
labels.notes: Unmarked and partial. These are the proof's steps and an assembly that carries the cited inputs, not the anchor. CONCLUSION. M.Y g ≤ −M.infF g (fun _ => c_N) is eq:upper-bound (l.497–498), with F_g = F^{(c_N)} and the inf over Adm (OQ-44). The extra conjunct Y = c·Vol^{2/N} is the value printed at l.724. STEPS. le_neg_infF_of_gluing and GluingInput.le_neg_infF give l.724–726: they drop the last term (proved ≤ 0) and use inf F ≤ F(u), since u is Adm and F ≥ 0 makes the set bounded below. kobM_mul_le_neg_infF is the limit of l.728. Its inputs are tendsto_kobM (kobM is 1-Lipschitz in R for the sup distance), tendsto_vol_of_uniformlyClose, and the strict tendsto_infF_of_uniformlyClose (lem:stability). It needs only the per-τ inequality eventually and a filter l ≠ ⊥. upper_bound_of_limit and upper_bound_of_gluings carry R_g ≡ c ≤ 0, pointwise. That is an added hypothesis relative to l.495, disclosed as the finding and marked ⚠ in the checklist. The _of_pos forms replace it with hpos : 0 < infF_g(c_N). That is lem:positivity (l.715–718), carried as a hypothesis and not proved, and it is exactly the model's form of the lemma. CARRIED INPUTS. The family gs with UniformlyClose (η τ) g g̃_τ, η → 0, |R_{g̃_τ} − R_g| ≤ δ_τ → 0 and MinimalBoundary (gs i) is lem:gluing (l.687), stated faithfully in the OQ-44 reading of 'uniformly'. Per τ, GluingInput gives y_nonpos, i.e. Y_[ḡ_τ](Σ̄) ≤ 0, from σ(Σ̄) ≤ 0 (l.724). bdryYamabe at β = c_N is fact (iv) plus 'by definition of YB', because ḡ_τ|_{D_j} lies in the flat-ball class. yamabe, law, flip and bmatch are as in lem:gluing-estimate. Asking 'for every i' rather than eventually in the assemblies costs nothing, since one can pass to the subtype with the comap filter. Joint satisfiability is not witnessed in the file. The auditor's probe builds a GluingInput at β = c_3 on the toy and applies upper_bound_of_gluings to the constant family, and it elaborates (minor finding 1). FINDING l.724 CHECKED, TRUE. prop:nonpositive (l.476–479, label l.477) assumes 'Σ̄ enlargeable' and positive boundary Yamabe classes. thm:upper-bound (l.493–500) assumes σ(Σ̄) ≤ 0, CSC, a minimal boundary and conformally round B_j. Conformally round B_j give the positivity of the boundary classes, so only enlargeability is missing. None of thm:upper-bound's hypotheses states R_g ≤ 0, so 'or directly by hypothesis' has no referent. The K3 argument is standard and correctly labelled 'argued, not formalized'. σ(K3) = 0 because K3 is Ricci-flat and admits no PSC metric (Â ≠ 0). It is simply connected, hence not enlargeable. Without R_g ≤ 0 the limit at l.728 is min(0,R_g)·Vol^{2/N}, and lem:kobayashi (a)'s 'EH = Y' needs R_g ≤ 0, so the citation is load-bearing. The repair is sound and is not circular. lem:gluing-estimate on g̃_τ uses m_τ = min(0, min R_{g̃_τ}) and needs no sign of R_g. The limit gives min(0,c)·V^{2/N} ≤ −inf F_g < 0. That excludes c ≥ 0, so c < 0 and Y_eq_const_mul applies. An empty X is excluded by the same inequality. lem:positivity is used in the paper's own setting (connected Σ, punctures, so ∂Σ ≠ ∅), which the paper already uses for cor:negative at l.728. The grading 'minor, statement unaffected' is right. A ledger observation for curation, not about this work: thm:upper-bound's row has proof: null (the REPORT notes this), and cor:negative's row links proof 'Yamabegap.tex:731' with span [731, 742]. That is the first-variation proof of rem:sign. The proof of cor:negative is l.723–729.

build.details: BUILD. From lean-yamabe/, `taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true scaffold/YamabeScaffold/Gluing.lean` exits 0 with no output. No lake build was run. The strict oleans predate this target: Kobayashi 23:48:57, Quotient 20:04:04, Stability 20:04:08. YamabeScaffold/Gluing.olean (02:10:14) is newer than its source (02:09:52), consistent with the REPORT's module-only build. SORRY AND TOKENS. grep finds zero hits for sorry, admit, axiom, unsafe, native_decide, implemented_by, extern, set_option, opaque and @[. The file imports only Yamabe.Kobayashi and Yamabe.Stability (strict, Mathlib-only), and every declaration is in namespace Yamabe. AXIOMS. The probe was /tmp/audit-gluing/Probe.lean, deleted afterwards: the source plus `#print axioms` for all 50 names in REPORT decls ∪ extra_decls. Those are exactly the file's 50 top-level declarations, set-equal. Each depends on exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. SATISFIABILITY PROBES. /tmp/audit-gluing/Sat.lean, deleted, gave standard axioms with no sorryAx. (a) A GluingInput toyModel Bool (Bool → ℝ) gT (fun _ => c_3) on the toy. The data: g = gT with G = 1, R ≡ −1 − 2c_3, H ≡ 0. h̄|_Σ has R ≡ −1, H ≡ −c_3. h̄|_{D_0} has R ≡ −1, H ≡ c_3, so EHB(D_0) = −2 + 4c_3 ≥ c_3. The rest is u = 1, y = −4^{2/3}, c = −1, glued by the identity. ConformalLaw holds there, since both sides equal −2 − 4c_3. toyModel.upper_bound_of_gluings then elaborated with ι = Unit, l = ⊤, gs ≡ gT and η = δ = 0. So the hypotheses of le_neg_infF_of_gluing, GluingInput and the assembly are jointly satisfiable. (b) gluing_estimate_YB elaborated on the same data with g_0 having R ≡ 0, H ≡ c_3 − 1/2, ψ_0 = 1 and ConformalLawB (both sides 4c_3 − 2). BddBelow holds by 0, since every competitor's confAction is ≥ 0. Not probed: hpos (lem:positivity) on the toy, which _of_pos carries. It is the paper's lemma and is mathematically true there by compactness.

findings.what: The file's only witness, toy_gluing_estimate, covers Filling.gluing_estimate, and its β_0 = EHB(D_0, toyCurved) = −2. It therefore cannot witness the β = c_N inputs on which thm:upper-bound's steps rest: BoundaryYamabe hb (fun _ => c_N) in le_neg_infF_of_gluing, GluingInput and upper_bound_of_gluings[_of_pos]. Nor does it witness gluing_estimate_YB's extra inputs (ConformalLawB, AdmB, BddBelow). The REPORT's claim is accurate as worded, since it says 'its hypotheses', meaning gluing_estimate's. The auditor's probe shows the missing ones are jointly satisfiable too (build.details), so nothing is vacuous. But the file does not show it.
